paragraphs.es: Me llamo Ana y tengo veinte años. Vivo en Puebla, una ciudad de México, con mi familia. Mi casa es pequeña, pero me gusta mucho.
paragraphs.en: My name is Ana and I'm twenty years old. I live in Puebla, a city in Mexico, with my family. My house is small, but I like it a lot.

paragraphs.es: Mi mamá es maestra y mi papá trabaja en un banco. Tengo un hermano, Luis. Él tiene doce años y le gusta el fútbol. Los domingos comemos juntos en casa de mi abuela.
paragraphs.en: My mom is a teacher and my dad works at a bank. I have a brother, Luis. He's twelve and he likes soccer. On Sundays we eat together at my grandmother's house.

questions.en: Where does Ana live?
questions.why: Ana lives in Puebla, a city in Mexico.

questions.en: What does Ana's mom do?
questions.why: Her mom is a teacher. Her dad is the one who works at a bank.

questions.en: How old is Luis?
questions.why: Luis is twelve. Ana is the one who is twenty.

questions.en: When do they eat together?
questions.why: They eat at the grandmother's house on Sundays.

paragraphs.es: Hoy es sábado y Rosa va al mercado con su hija. El mercado está cerca de la plaza y siempre hay mucha gente. Rosa necesita tomates, cebollas y aguacates.
paragraphs.en: Today is Saturday and Rosa is going to the market with her daughter. The market is near the square and there are always a lot of people. Rosa needs tomatoes, onions and avocados.

paragraphs.es: Rosa pregunta: «¿Cuánto cuestan los aguacates?» El vendedor dice: «Tres quetzales cada uno.» Rosa compra cuatro. Su hija quiere una fruta y Rosa le compra un mango. Esta noche van a comer guacamole en casa.
paragraphs.en: Rosa asks, "How much are the avocados?" The seller says, "Three quetzales each." Rosa buys four. Her daughter wants a piece of fruit and Rosa buys her a mango. Tonight they're going to eat guacamole at home.

questions.en: Who does Rosa go to the market with?
questions.why: Rosa goes with her daughter.

questions.en: How many avocados does Rosa buy?
questions.why: She buys four. Three is the price of each one, in quetzales.

questions.en: What does the daughter want?
questions.why: She wants a piece of fruit, so Rosa buys her a mango.

questions.en: What are they going to eat tonight?
questions.why: "Van a comer" talks about the plan for tonight: guacamole at home.

paragraphs.es: Carlos vive en San Juan, Puerto Rico. Se levanta a las seis de la mañana y toma café con leche. Después sale a caminar por la playa con su perro, Coco.
paragraphs.en: Carlos lives in San Juan, Puerto Rico. He gets up at six in the morning and has coffee with milk. Then he goes out for a walk on the beach with his dog, Coco.

paragraphs.es: A las ocho va a trabajar. Carlos es enfermero en un hospital grande. Trabaja mucho, pero le gusta ayudar a la gente. Por la noche está cansado. Cena, lee un poco y se acuesta a las diez.
paragraphs.en: At eight he goes to work. Carlos is a nurse at a big hospital. He works a lot, but he likes helping people. At night he's tired. He has dinner, reads a little and goes to bed at ten.

questions.en: What time does Carlos get up?
questions.why: He gets up at six. He goes to work at eight and to bed at ten.

questions.en: Who is Coco?
questions.why: Coco is the dog Carlos walks on the beach.

questions.en: Where does Carlos work?
questions.why: He's a nurse at a big hospital.

questions.en: How is Carlos at night?
questions.why: "Está cansado" means he's tired.

paragraphs.es: Sofía y Mateo son amigos y viven en Bogotá. Mañana es sábado y no tienen clases. Van a ir a un parque grande con sus amigos.
paragraphs.en: Sofía and Mateo are friends and they live in Bogotá. Tomorrow is Saturday and they don't have classes. They're going to go to a big park with their friends.

paragraphs.es: Sofía va a llevar su guitarra y Mateo va a llevar la comida. En Bogotá hace frío por la mañana y a veces llueve, entonces Sofía también va a llevar una chaqueta. Por la tarde, si no llueve, todos van a jugar fútbol.
paragraphs.en: Sofía is going to bring her guitar and Mateo is going to bring the food. In Bogotá it's cold in the morning and sometimes it rains, so Sofía is also going to bring a jacket. In the afternoon, if it doesn't rain, they're all going to play soccer.

questions.en: Why don't they have classes tomorrow?
questions.why: Tomorrow is Saturday, so there are no classes.

questions.en: What is Mateo going to bring?
questions.why: Mateo brings the food. The guitar and the jacket are Sofía's.

questions.en: Why is Sofía bringing a jacket?
questions.why: Mornings in Bogotá are cold, and it sometimes rains.

questions.q: ¿Qué van a hacer por la tarde si no llueve?
questions.en: What will they do in the afternoon if it doesn't rain?
questions.why: "Si no llueve, todos van a jugar fútbol."

paragraphs.es: Camila vive en Medellín y trabaja en una oficina. Todos los días, después del trabajo, estudia inglés en una escuela de idiomas. Siempre llega temprano a la clase.
paragraphs.en: Camila lives in Medellín and works in an office. Every day, after work, she studies English at a language school. She always gets to class early.

paragraphs.es: En la clase, los estudiantes leen, escriben y hablan mucho. Andrés, el maestro, pregunta y Camila contesta. A veces no comprende una palabra y busca la respuesta en el libro.
paragraphs.en: In class, the students read, write and talk a lot. Andrés, the teacher, asks and Camila answers. Sometimes she doesn't understand a word and looks for the answer in the book.

paragraphs.es: Mañana hay examen. Hoy Camila estudia con su compañero Mateo en la biblioteca y después come en casa.
paragraphs.en: Tomorrow there's a test. Today Camila studies with her classmate Mateo at the library, and afterwards she eats at home.

questions.en: Where does Camila work?
questions.why: Camila works in an office. She studies at the school after work.

questions.en: What does Camila study?
questions.why: She studies English at a language school.

questions.en: Who is Andrés?
questions.why: Andrés is the teacher. Mateo is her classmate.

questions.q: ¿Qué hace Camila cuando no comprende una palabra?
questions.en: What does Camila do when she doesn't understand a word?
choices: Busca la respuesta en el libro
questions.answer: Busca la respuesta en el libro
questions.why: When she doesn't understand a word, she looks for the answer in the book.

paragraphs.es: Antigua es una ciudad pequeña y bonita de Guatemala. Las calles son viejas y las casas son blancas, amarillas o rojas. Hay montañas grandes cerca de la ciudad.
paragraphs.en: Antigua is a small, pretty city in Guatemala. The streets are old and the houses are white, yellow or red. There are big mountains near the city.

paragraphs.es: Elena vive en una casa vieja con una ventana grande. En su cuarto hay una mesa negra, dos sillas rojas y muchos libros. Los libros son nuevos, pero la mesa es muy vieja: es de su abuela. En la pared, Elena tiene un mapa de la ciudad.
paragraphs.en: Elena lives in an old house with a big window. In her room there's a black table, two red chairs and lots of books. The books are new, but the table is very old: it was her grandmother's. On the wall, Elena has a map of the city.

questions.en: What is Antigua like?
questions.why: Antigua is a small, pretty city. It's the mountains near it that are big.

questions.en: What color are the chairs?
questions.why: The two chairs are red. The table is the black one.

questions.en: Whose table is it?
questions.why: The table is very old and was her grandmother's.

questions.en: What's on the wall?
questions.why: Elena has a map of the city on the wall. Note it's un mapa: mapa is masculine, though it ends in -a.

paragraphs.es: Gabriela y Paula son hermanas y son de Santo Domingo. Gabriela es alta, simpática y muy trabajadora. Paula es baja y tranquila, y es muy inteligente.
paragraphs.en: Gabriela and Paula are sisters and they're from Santo Domingo. Gabriela is tall, friendly and very hard-working. Paula is short and calm, and she's very smart.

paragraphs.es: Hoy es lunes y las dos están ocupadas. Gabriela está en la oficina y está cansada, porque hay mucho trabajo. Paula está en casa. Está enferma y un poco triste.
paragraphs.en: Today is Monday and they're both busy. Gabriela is at the office and she's tired, because there's a lot of work. Paula is at home. She's sick and a little sad.

paragraphs.es: Por la noche, Gabriela llega a casa con sopa y chocolate. Ahora Paula está contenta.
paragraphs.en: In the evening, Gabriela gets home with soup and chocolate. Now Paula is happy.

questions.en: Where are Gabriela and Paula from?
questions.why: They're from Santo Domingo. Where someone is from takes ser: son de Santo Domingo.

questions.en: What is Paula like?
questions.why: ¿Cómo es? asks what she's like, which takes ser: she's short and calm. Sick and sad is how she is today, with estar.

questions.en: Where is Gabriela today?
questions.why: Gabriela is at the office. Where someone is takes estar.

questions.en: How is Paula at the end?
questions.why: After the soup and chocolate, Paula is happy. ¿Cómo está? asks how she feels right now.

paragraphs.es: Diego vive en Valparaíso. Los sábados duerme hasta las nueve y después desayuna con su familia. Su papá prefiere café, pero Diego quiere chocolate caliente.
paragraphs.en: Diego lives in Valparaíso. On Saturdays he sleeps until nine and then has breakfast with his family. His dad prefers coffee, but Diego wants hot chocolate.

paragraphs.es: Por la tarde, juega al fútbol con sus amigos en el parque. El partido empieza a las tres, pero no pueden jugar mucho tiempo, porque el parque cierra a las seis.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon, he plays soccer with his friends in the park. The game starts at three, but they can't play for long, because the park closes at six.

paragraphs.es: Diego vuelve a casa antes de la cena. El lunes tiene un examen y no entiende bien los problemas, pero hoy no quiere pensar en eso.
paragraphs.en: Diego comes back home before dinner. On Monday he has a test and doesn't really understand the problems, but today he doesn't want to think about that.

questions.q: ¿Hasta qué hora duerme Diego los sábados?
questions.en: Until what time does Diego sleep on Saturdays?
questions.why: He sleeps until nine. The game starts at three and the park closes at six.

questions.en: What does Diego want at breakfast?
questions.why: Diego wants hot chocolate. His dad is the one who prefers coffee.

questions.q: ¿Por qué no pueden jugar mucho tiempo?
questions.en: Why can't they play for long?
choices: Porque el parque cierra a las seis
questions.answer: Porque el parque cierra a las seis
questions.why: The park closes at six, so the game can't go on for long.

questions.en: What doesn't Diego understand well?
questions.why: He has a test on Monday and doesn't really understand the problems.

paragraphs.es: A Sofía le encanta visitar a su abuela en San Juan. A su abuela le gusta mucho cocinar. Su pescado con arroz es delicioso, y de postre siempre hay pastel.
paragraphs.en: Sofía loves visiting her grandmother in San Juan. Her grandmother really likes to cook. Her fish with rice is delicious, and for dessert there's always cake.

paragraphs.es: A Sofía no le gustan las verduras, pero le encantan las frutas. A su hermano Juan le interesan los deportes, y a los dos les gusta la música.
paragraphs.en: Sofía doesn't like vegetables, but she loves fruit. Her brother Juan is interested in sports, and they both like music.

paragraphs.es: Después de la comida, a la abuela le duelen los pies, pero no le importa. ¡Le gusta ver a sus nietos contentos!
paragraphs.en: After the meal, the grandmother's feet hurt, but she doesn't mind. She likes seeing her grandchildren happy!

questions.q: ¿Qué le gusta hacer a la abuela?
questions.en: What does the grandmother like to do?
questions.why: A su abuela le gusta mucho cocinar: she really likes to cook.

questions.en: What doesn't Sofía like?
questions.why: No le gustan las verduras. Gustan agrees with verduras, which is plural.

questions.en: What is Juan interested in?
questions.why: A Juan le interesan los deportes: he's interested in sports.

questions.en: What hurts the grandmother?
questions.why: Le duelen los pies: her feet hurt, but she doesn't mind.

paragraphs.es: Mañana empiezan las vacaciones de verano, y la familia de Carmen va a viajar a la costa de Ecuador. Van a ir en autobús. Carmen va a llevar su libro favorito.
paragraphs.en: Tomorrow summer vacation starts, and Carmen's family is going to travel to the coast of Ecuador. They're going to go by bus. Carmen is going to bring her favorite book.

paragraphs.es: En la playa, sus papás van a descansar y su hermano Luis va a nadar todo el día. Carmen va a visitar el museo y el mercado del pueblo. El sábado van a cenar en un restaurante: es el cumpleaños de su mamá.
paragraphs.en: At the beach, her parents are going to rest and her brother Luis is going to swim all day. Carmen is going to visit the museum and the town market. On Saturday they're going to have dinner at a restaurant: it's her mom's birthday.

questions.en: Where is the family going to travel?
questions.why: They're going to the coast of Ecuador.

questions.en: How are they going to get there?
questions.why: Van a ir en autobús: they're going by bus.

questions.en: What is Luis going to do?
questions.why: Luis is going to swim all day. Carmen is the one visiting the museum.

questions.q: ¿Por qué van a cenar en un restaurante?
questions.en: Why are they going to have dinner at a restaurant?
choices: Es el cumpleaños de su mamá
questions.answer: Es el cumpleaños de su mamá
questions.why: On Saturday it's Carmen's mom's birthday.

paragraphs.es: El año pasado, Daniela viajó a Perú con su hermana. Primero llegaron a Lima y pasaron dos días allí. Comieron ceviche, visitaron el centro histórico y caminaron por el malecón, frente al mar.
paragraphs.en: Last year, Daniela traveled to Peru with her sister. First they arrived in Lima and spent two days there. They ate ceviche, visited the historic center and walked along the seafront promenade, facing the ocean.

paragraphs.es: Después tomaron un avión a Cusco. La ciudad está a más de tres mil metros de altura, y el primer día Daniela se sintió mal. Le dolía la cabeza y estaba muy cansada. Una señora del hotel le preparó un té caliente y le dijo que debía descansar.
paragraphs.en: Then they took a plane to Cusco. The city is more than three thousand meters high, and on the first day Daniela felt sick. Her head hurt and she was very tired. A woman at the hotel made her a hot tea and told her she should rest.

paragraphs.es: Al día siguiente se sentía mejor. Las dos hermanas subieron a Machu Picchu muy temprano. Había mucha niebla, pero poco a poco salió el sol y vieron las ruinas. Daniela dice que fue el mejor día de su vida.
paragraphs.en: The next day she felt better. The two sisters went up to Machu Picchu very early. There was a lot of fog, but little by little the sun came out and they saw the ruins. Daniela says it was the best day of her life.

questions.en: Who did Daniela travel with?
questions.why: She traveled with her sister.

questions.en: What did they eat in Lima?
questions.why: They ate ceviche during their two days in Lima.

questions.q: ¿Por qué se sintió mal Daniela en Cusco?
questions.en: Why did Daniela feel sick in Cusco?
questions.why: The passage mentions Cusco is over 3,000 meters high just before she feels sick.

questions.en: What happened at Machu Picchu?
choices: Salió el sol poco a poco
questions.answer: Salió el sol poco a poco
questions.why: There was fog at first, then the sun came out and they saw the ruins.

paragraphs.es: Cuando mi abuelo era niño, vivía en un pueblo pequeño cerca de Santiago, en la República Dominicana. Su familia no tenía televisor ni teléfono. La casa estaba al lado de un río, y él se bañaba allí con sus hermanos casi todos los días.
paragraphs.en: When my grandfather was a boy, he lived in a small town near Santiago, in the Dominican Republic. His family didn't have a TV or a telephone. The house was next to a river, and he swam there with his brothers and sisters almost every day.

paragraphs.es: Por la mañana ayudaba a su padre en el campo. Por la tarde jugaba béisbol con los otros niños del pueblo. No tenían guantes de verdad, así que usaban guantes hechos de cartón. Por la noche, toda la familia se sentaba afuera y escuchaba la radio.
paragraphs.en: In the morning he helped his father in the fields. In the afternoon he played baseball with the other kids in town. They didn't have real gloves, so they used gloves made of cardboard. At night, the whole family sat outside and listened to the radio.

paragraphs.es: Una vez, cuando tenía doce años, un equipo de la capital llegó al pueblo. Les faltaba un jugador y mi abuelo jugó con ellos. Ganaron el partido, y el entrenador le regaló un guante de cuero. Todavía lo tiene.
paragraphs.en: Once, when he was twelve, a team from the capital came to town. They were short a player and my grandfather played with them. They won the game, and the coach gave him a leather glove. He still has it.

questions.en: Where was the grandfather's house?
questions.why: The house was next to a river, in a small town near Santiago.

questions.q: ¿Qué hacía el abuelo por las mañanas?
questions.en: What did the grandfather do in the mornings?
questions.why: The imperfect shows a routine: every morning he helped his father in the fields.

questions.q: ¿De qué eran los guantes de los niños?
questions.en: What were the kids' gloves made of?
questions.why: They had no real gloves, so they used cardboard ones.

questions.q: ¿Por qué jugó el abuelo con el equipo de la capital?
questions.en: Why did the grandfather play with the team from the capital?
questions.why: "Les faltaba un jugador" means they were one player short.

paragraphs.es: El martes, Valentina salió tarde de su casa en Santiago de Chile. Corrió hasta la parada y subió a la micro, como le dicen al autobús en Chile. Había mucha gente y tuvo que ir de pie.
paragraphs.en: On Tuesday, Valentina left her house in Santiago, Chile, late. She ran to the stop and got on the micro, as they call the bus in Chile. There were a lot of people and she had to stand.

paragraphs.es: Cuando llegó a la oficina, buscó su celular en la mochila, pero no estaba. Lo buscó en los bolsillos y tampoco estaba allí. Se puso muy nerviosa, porque tenía todas sus fotos y sus contactos en ese teléfono.
paragraphs.en: When she got to the office, she looked for her cell phone in her backpack, but it wasn't there. She looked for it in her pockets and it wasn't there either. She got very nervous, because she had all her photos and contacts on that phone.

paragraphs.es: Una compañera llamó a su número. Después de varios segundos, un hombre contestó: «Hola, soy el chofer de la micro. Encontré este celular debajo de un asiento.» Esa tarde, Valentina fue a buscarlo y le dio las gracias.
paragraphs.en: A coworker called her number. After several seconds, a man answered: "Hello, I'm the driver of the micro. I found this cell phone under a seat." That afternoon, Valentina went to get it and thanked him.

questions.en: What is a micro in Chile?
questions.why: "Como le dicen al autobús en Chile" explains the word.

questions.en: Where did Valentina look for her cell phone?
choices: En la mochila y los bolsillos
questions.answer: En la mochila y los bolsillos
questions.why: She checked her backpack first, then her pockets.

questions.en: Why did she get nervous?
choices: Porque tenía sus fotos en el teléfono
questions.answer: Porque tenía sus fotos en el teléfono
questions.why: Her photos and contacts were all on the phone.

questions.en: Who found the cell phone?
questions.why: The driver found it under a seat. The coworker only called the number.

paragraphs.es: La semana pasada fue el cumpleaños de don Ernesto, un señor de setenta años que vive en Heredia, Costa Rica. Sus hijos querían hacerle una fiesta sorpresa, pero era difícil, porque él siempre sabía todo lo que pasaba en la familia.
paragraphs.en: Last week was the birthday of don Ernesto, a seventy-year-old man who lives in Heredia, Costa Rica. His children wanted to throw him a surprise party, but it was hard, because he always knew everything that went on in the family.

paragraphs.es: Por eso, su hija Marta lo invitó a tomar café en el centro. Mientras ellos hablaban, los demás llevaron comida, flores y sillas a la casa. Todos trabajaban rápido, porque no tenían mucho tiempo.
paragraphs.en: So his daughter Marta invited him for coffee downtown. While they talked, the others brought food, flowers and chairs to the house. Everyone worked fast, because they didn't have much time.

paragraphs.es: Cuando don Ernesto y Marta volvieron, la casa estaba oscura. Él abrió la puerta, encendió la luz y todos gritaron: «¡Sorpresa!» Don Ernesto se rio y lloró al mismo tiempo. Después comieron arroz con pollo y bailaron hasta muy tarde. «Ustedes son increíbles», les dijo a sus hijos.
paragraphs.en: When don Ernesto and Marta came back, the house was dark. He opened the door, turned on the light and everyone shouted, "Surprise!" Don Ernesto laughed and cried at the same time. Then they ate chicken and rice and danced until very late. "You're incredible," he told his children.

words.en: respectful title used before a man's first name

questions.q: ¿Por qué era difícil hacer la fiesta sorpresa?
questions.en: Why was the surprise party hard to do?
choices: Porque don Ernesto lo sabía todo
questions.answer: Porque don Ernesto lo sabía todo
questions.why: He always knew everything that went on in the family.

questions.en: What did Marta do?
questions.why: She took him out for coffee so the others could set up.

questions.en: How was the house when they came back?
questions.why: The house was dark, so he had to turn on the light.

questions.q: ¿Qué hizo don Ernesto después del grito de «¡Sorpresa!»?
questions.en: What did don Ernesto do after the shout of "Surprise!"?
questions.why: He laughed and cried at the same time.

paragraphs.es: Valentina vive en la Ciudad de Panamá y trabaja en un hotel. Todos los días se despierta a las cinco y media, cuando suena el despertador. No se levanta enseguida: se queda cinco minutos más en la cama.
paragraphs.en: Valentina lives in Panama City and works at a hotel. Every day she wakes up at five thirty, when the alarm clock goes off. She doesn't get up right away: she stays in bed five more minutes.

paragraphs.es: Después se ducha con agua fría, se lava la cara y se lava los dientes. Luego se viste: se pone una camisa blanca, un pantalón negro y unos zapatos cómodos. Se peina delante del espejo y sale de casa a las seis y cuarto.
paragraphs.en: Then she showers with cold water, washes her face and brushes her teeth. Next she gets dressed: she puts on a white shirt, black pants and comfortable shoes. She combs her hair in front of the mirror and leaves home at a quarter past six.

paragraphs.es: Su hermano Mateo es muy diferente. Él se acuesta tarde y nunca se despierta temprano. Los sábados, los dos se quedan en casa y se divierten juntos, y Valentina por fin puede dormir hasta las diez.
paragraphs.en: Her brother Mateo is very different. He goes to bed late and never wakes up early. On Saturdays they both stay home and have fun together, and Valentina can finally sleep until ten.

questions.en: What time does Valentina wake up?
questions.why: She wakes up at five thirty. She leaves home at a quarter past six, and sleeps until ten only on Saturdays.

questions.en: What does she do after showering?
choices: Se lava la cara y los dientes
questions.answer: Se lava la cara y los dientes
questions.why: After the shower she washes her face and brushes her teeth, then gets dressed.

questions.q: ¿Qué ropa se pone para el trabajo?
questions.en: What clothes does she put on for work?
choices: Una camisa blanca y un pantalón negro
Una camisa negra y un pantalón blanco
questions.answer: Una camisa blanca y un pantalón negro
questions.why: Se pone una camisa blanca y un pantalón negro: the shirt is white and the pants are black.

questions.en: How is Mateo different?
choices: Se acuesta tarde y se despierta tarde
questions.answer: Se acuesta tarde y se despierta tarde
questions.why: Mateo goes to bed late and never wakes up early. Valentina is the one who works at the hotel.

paragraphs.es: El verano pasado, Daniela y su amiga Sofía viajaron de Lima a Bolivia. Compraron los boletos en octubre y prepararon las maletas una semana antes. El vuelo salió muy temprano y llegó a La Paz a las nueve de la mañana.
paragraphs.en: Last summer, Daniela and her friend Sofía traveled from Lima to Bolivia. They bought the tickets in October and packed their suitcases a week before. The flight left very early and arrived in La Paz at nine in the morning.

paragraphs.es: En La Paz, caminaron mucho por el centro y visitaron un mercado enorme. Probaron la comida típica y tomaron muchas fotos.
paragraphs.en: In La Paz, they walked a lot around the center and visited a huge market. They tried the local food and took lots of photos.

paragraphs.es: Después, tomaron un autobús al lago Titicaca. Allí pasaron dos noches en un hotel pequeño, subieron una montaña y miraron el lago desde arriba. Esa noche, Daniela escribió en su cuaderno: «El mejor viaje de mi vida». El domingo volvieron a Lima, cansadas pero muy contentas.
paragraphs.en: Then they took a bus to Lake Titicaca. There they spent two nights in a small hotel, climbed a mountain and looked at the lake from above. That night, Daniela wrote in her notebook: "The best trip of my life." On Sunday they went back to Lima, tired but very happy.

questions.en: When did they buy the tickets?
questions.why: They bought the tickets in October. They packed a week before the trip.

questions.en: Which city did the flight arrive in?
questions.why: The flight left Lima and arrived in La Paz at nine in the morning.

questions.en: Where did they spend two nights?
choices: En un hotel pequeño cerca del lago
En el mercado de La Paz
questions.answer: En un hotel pequeño cerca del lago
questions.why: At Lake Titicaca they spent two nights in a small hotel.

questions.en: What did Daniela write in her notebook?
choices: El mejor viaje de mi vida
questions.answer: El mejor viaje de mi vida
questions.why: She wrote «El mejor viaje de mi vida»: the best trip of her life.

paragraphs.es: El sábado pasado fue la boda de mi prima Elena en Oaxaca. Toda la familia vino de lejos: mis tíos hicieron un viaje de diez horas en carro, y mi abuela vino en avión desde Tijuana.
paragraphs.en: Last Saturday was my cousin Elena's wedding in Oaxaca. The whole family came from far away: my aunt and uncle made a ten-hour trip by car, and my grandmother came by plane from Tijuana.

paragraphs.es: La ceremonia estuvo muy bonita. Cuando los novios dijeron «sí», mi tía no pudo dejar de llorar. Después hubo una fiesta enorme con música y baile. Yo traje el regalo de mi familia, una caja con platos y vasos, y mi papá puso la caja en la mesa de los regalos.
paragraphs.en: The ceremony was very beautiful. When the bride and groom said "yes," my aunt couldn't stop crying. Afterwards there was a huge party with music and dancing. I brought my family's gift, a box of plates and glasses, and my dad put the box on the gift table.

paragraphs.es: A medianoche, mi hermano quiso cantar una canción para los novios, pero cantó muy mal y todos se rieron. Al final de la noche, supimos una gran noticia: ¡los novios van a vivir en nuestra ciudad! Fue una noche increíble.
paragraphs.en: At midnight, my brother wanted to sing a song for the couple, but he sang very badly and everyone laughed. At the end of the night, we found out some big news: the couple is going to live in our city! It was an incredible night.

questions.q: ¿Cómo vino la abuela a la boda?
questions.en: How did the grandmother come to the wedding?
questions.why: The grandmother came by plane from Tijuana. The aunt and uncle were the ones who came by car.

questions.en: Who couldn't stop crying?
questions.why: Mi tía no pudo dejar de llorar when the couple said yes.

questions.q: ¿Qué regalo trajo la persona que cuenta la historia?
questions.en: What gift did the person telling the story bring?
choices: Una caja con platos y vasos
questions.answer: Una caja con platos y vasos
questions.why: Traje el regalo de mi familia: a box of plates and glasses.

questions.q: ¿Qué noticia supieron al final de la noche?
questions.en: What news did they find out at the end of the night?
choices: Los novios van a vivir en su ciudad
La abuela va a vivir con ellos
Hay otra boda el próximo mes
questions.answer: Los novios van a vivir en su ciudad
questions.why: Supimos una gran noticia: the couple is going to live in their city. Saber in the preterite means to find out.

paragraphs.es: Mi abuelo Ernesto siempre me cuenta cómo era su vida cuando era niño. Vivía en un pueblo pequeño de El Salvador, cerca de un río. Su casa tenía un patio grande con árboles de mango, y allí jugaba todas las tardes con sus hermanos.
paragraphs.en: My grandpa Ernesto always tells me what his life was like when he was a boy. He lived in a small village in El Salvador, near a river. His house had a big yard with mango trees, and he played there every afternoon with his brothers and sisters.

paragraphs.es: No tenían muchos juguetes. Normalmente jugaban con una pelota vieja o hacían carros de madera. Su perro, Canelo, siempre corría detrás de ellos. De vez en cuando, iban al río a nadar con los otros niños del barrio.
paragraphs.en: They didn't have many toys. Usually they played with an old ball or made wooden cars. Their dog, Canelo, always ran after them. Every now and then, they went to the river to swim with the other kids from the neighborhood.

paragraphs.es: Los domingos, toda la familia comía en casa de su abuela. Ella cocinaba tortillas y frijoles, y los vecinos venían de visita. Mi abuelo dice que era un niño tímido, pero feliz. «No teníamos mucho», me dice, «pero nunca nos faltaba nada».
paragraphs.en: On Sundays, the whole family ate at his grandmother's house. She cooked tortillas and beans, and the neighbors came over to visit. My grandpa says he was a shy boy, but a happy one. "We didn't have much," he tells me, "but we never went without anything."

questions.q: ¿Dónde vivía el abuelo cuando era niño?
questions.en: Where did the grandfather live when he was a boy?
choices: En un pueblo cerca de un río
questions.answer: En un pueblo cerca de un río
questions.why: Vivía en un pueblo pequeño, cerca de un río.

questions.en: What did they usually play with?
questions.why: They didn't have many toys, so they usually played with an old ball or made wooden cars.

questions.en: Who was Canelo?
questions.why: Canelo was their dog, who always ran after them.

questions.en: What did the family do on Sundays?
choices: Comía en casa de la abuela
questions.answer: Comía en casa de la abuela
questions.why: On Sundays the whole family ate at his grandmother's house. The imperfect, comía, says it happened regularly.

paragraphs.es: Era un sábado de enero y hacía mucho calor en Asunción. El cielo estaba azul y no había viento. Martina y su hermano Pablo estaban en el parque con su perro. Pablo jugaba con la pelota y Martina leía un libro debajo de un árbol.
paragraphs.en: It was a Saturday in January and it was very hot in Asunción. The sky was blue and there was no wind. Martina and her brother Pablo were in the park with their dog. Pablo was playing with the ball and Martina was reading a book under a tree.

paragraphs.es: De repente, el cielo se puso oscuro y empezó a hacer mucho viento. Martina cerró el libro y llamó a su hermano. Entonces empezó a llover muy fuerte. Los dos corrieron hacia la casa, pero el perro no quería caminar: tenía miedo de la tormenta.
paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the sky went dark and it got very windy. Martina closed the book and called her brother. Then it started to rain very hard. They both ran toward the house, but the dog didn't want to walk: it was afraid of the storm.

paragraphs.es: Cuando por fin llegaron a casa, estaban mojados de pies a cabeza. Su mamá preparó chocolate caliente para los dos. Una hora después, salió el sol otra vez, y el perro, ya tranquilo, se durmió en el sofá.
paragraphs.en: When they finally got home, they were wet from head to toe. Their mom made hot chocolate for the two of them. An hour later, the sun came out again, and the dog, calm now, fell asleep on the sofa.

questions.en: What was the weather like at first?
choices: Hacía calor y el cielo estaba azul
questions.answer: Hacía calor y el cielo estaba azul
questions.why: It was hot and the sky was blue. The imperfect sets the scene before anything happens.

questions.en: What was Martina doing in the park?
questions.why: Martina was reading a book. Pablo was the one playing with the ball.

questions.en: What happened suddenly?
questions.why: De repente, el cielo se puso oscuro: the preterite tells what happened and broke into the scene.

questions.q: ¿Por qué el perro no quería caminar?
questions.en: Why didn't the dog want to walk?
questions.why: The dog was afraid of the storm.

paragraphs.es: Andrés se mudó a un apartamento nuevo en Caracas la semana pasada. Tenía muchas cajas, así que llamó a su amiga Carmen y le pidió ayuda. Ella le dijo: «Claro, te ayudo el sábado».
paragraphs.en: Andrés moved to a new apartment in Caracas last week. He had lots of boxes, so he called his friend Carmen and asked her for help. She told him, "Sure, I'll help you on Saturday."

paragraphs.es: El sábado, Carmen llegó temprano y trajo a su hermano Luis. Los tres subieron las cajas al cuarto piso. Luis encontró una caja muy pesada y le preguntó a Andrés: «¿Qué hay aquí?». «Libros», le contestó Andrés. «Los voy a poner en la sala».
paragraphs.en: On Saturday, Carmen arrived early and brought her brother Luis. The three of them carried the boxes up to the fourth floor. Luis found a very heavy box and asked Andrés, "What's in here?" "Books," Andrés answered. "I'm going to put them in the living room."

paragraphs.es: Por la tarde, Andrés no encontraba sus llaves. Las buscó en todas las cajas. Al final, Carmen las vio en la cocina, dentro de una olla. Se las dio y todos se rieron. Para darles las gracias, Andrés les compró pizza.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon, Andrés couldn't find his keys. He looked for them in every box. In the end, Carmen saw them in the kitchen, inside a pot. She gave them to him and everyone laughed. To thank them, Andrés bought them pizza.

questions.en: What did Andrés ask Carmen for?
questions.why: He had lots of boxes, so he called Carmen y le pidió ayuda. Le stands for Carmen.

questions.en: What was in the heavy box?
questions.why: It was full of books. «Los voy a poner en la sala»: los stands for the books.

questions.en: Where did Carmen find the keys?
questions.why: Carmen las vio en la cocina, dentro de una olla. Las stands for the keys.

questions.q: ¿Qué les compró Andrés a sus amigos?
questions.en: What did Andrés buy his friends?
questions.why: To thank them, Andrés les compró pizza. Les stands for Carmen and Luis.

paragraphs.es: Querida Elena: Ya han pasado tres meses desde que llegué a Miami, y todavía no me acostumbro del todo. He encontrado trabajo en una panadería cubana, así que hablo español casi todo el día, pero quiero que mi inglés mejore. Por eso, me he inscrito en una clase nocturna dos veces por semana.
paragraphs.en: Dear Elena: Three months have already gone by since I arrived in Miami, and I'm still not fully used to it. I've found a job at a Cuban bakery, so I speak Spanish almost all day, but I want my English to improve. That's why I've signed up for a night class twice a week.

paragraphs.es: Lo más difícil es estar lejos de ustedes. Extraño los almuerzos de los domingos en Caracas, las bromas de papá y hasta el tráfico. Aquí todo queda lejos y sin carro es complicado moverse. Cuando tenga un poco más de dinero, me compraré uno usado.
paragraphs.en: The hardest part is being far from all of you. I miss Sunday lunches in Caracas, Dad's jokes and even the traffic. Everything is far away here, and without a car it's complicated to get around. When I have a little more money, I'll buy a used one.

paragraphs.es: No te preocupes por mí, porque estoy bien y he conocido a gente muy amable. Mi vecina, doña Carmen, siempre me trae comida y me pregunta por ustedes. Espero que mamá se sienta mejor y que puedan visitarme el próximo año. Si vienen, los llevaré a la playa. Te mando un abrazo muy fuerte. Tu hermano, Andrés.
paragraphs.en: Don't worry about me, because I'm fine and I've met very kind people. My neighbor, doña Carmen, always brings me food and asks about you all. I hope Mom feels better and that you can visit me next year. If you come, I'll take you to the beach. I'm sending you a big hug. Your brother, Andrés.

questions.q: ¿Por qué quiere Andrés tomar una clase nocturna?
questions.en: Why does Andrés want to take a night class?
questions.why: He speaks Spanish all day at work and wants his English to improve.

questions.q: ¿Qué es lo más difícil para Andrés?
questions.en: What is the hardest thing for Andrés?
questions.why: "Lo más difícil es estar lejos de ustedes."

questions.en: When is he going to buy a car?
questions.why: "Cuando tenga" uses the subjunctive because that moment hasn't happened yet.

questions.en: How does doña Carmen help Andrés?
questions.why: His neighbor always brings him food.

questions.en: What does Andrés hope for?
choices: Que su hermana le mande dinero
Que su papá se mude a Miami
questions.why: He hopes his mother feels better and that they can visit next year.

paragraphs.es: La familia Mejía ha cultivado café en las montañas de Honduras durante cuatro generaciones. Su finca es pequeña, pero produce un café excelente que se vende en tiendas de Europa y Estados Unidos. Sin embargo, en los últimos años el clima ha cambiado y las plantas se enferman con más frecuencia.
paragraphs.en: The Mejía family has grown coffee in the mountains of Honduras for four generations. Their farm is small, but it produces excellent coffee that is sold in stores in Europe and the United States. However, in recent years the climate has changed and the plants get sick more often.

paragraphs.es: Lucía, la hija menor, estudió agronomía en la universidad y volvió a la finca con algunas ideas nuevas. Quiere que su familia plante árboles que den sombra, porque así el café estará protegido del calor. Su padre no está seguro. Le preocupa que esos cambios cuesten demasiado y tarden años en dar resultados.
paragraphs.en: Lucía, the youngest daughter, studied agronomy at the university and came back to the farm with some new ideas. She wants her family to plant trees that give shade, because that way the coffee will be protected from the heat. Her father isn't sure. He worries that those changes will cost too much and take years to show results.

paragraphs.es: «Si no hacemos nada, perderemos la cosecha tarde o temprano», le dijo Lucía. Al final, decidieron probar en una parte de la finca. Plantarán los árboles este año, y en tres años sabrán si la idea funciona. Mientras tanto, Lucía ha empezado a vender café por internet, lo cual podría darles más ingresos.
paragraphs.en: "If we do nothing, we'll lose the harvest sooner or later," Lucía told him. In the end, they decided to try it on one part of the farm. They'll plant the trees this year, and in three years they'll know whether the idea works. In the meantime, Lucía has started selling coffee online, which could give them more income.

questions.en: What problem does the farm have?
questions.why: The climate has changed and the plants get sick more often.

questions.en: What does Lucía want to do?
questions.why: Shade would protect the coffee from the heat.

questions.en: What worries the father?
questions.why: He worries about the cost and how long results will take. "Le preocupa que" takes the subjunctive.

questions.en: What did they decide in the end?
choices: Probar en una parte de la finca
questions.answer: Probar en una parte de la finca
questions.why: They'll try it on one part and see the results in three years.

questions.en: What has Lucía started doing?
questions.why: "Ha empezado a" means she has started to. Selling online could bring in more income.

paragraphs.es: Camila trabaja como diseñadora en Quito y acaba de recibir una oferta de trabajo en Panamá. Ganaría casi el doble de lo que gana ahora, y la empresa le pagaría el viaje y el primer mes de alquiler. Es una gran oportunidad, pero no sabe qué hacer.
paragraphs.en: Camila works as a designer in Quito and has just received a job offer in Panama. She would earn almost double what she earns now, and the company would pay for the trip and the first month of rent. It's a great opportunity, but she doesn't know what to do.

paragraphs.es: Sus padres ya están mayores y ella los visita todas las semanas. Su novio, Tomás, tiene un negocio en Quito y no podría mudarse con ella. «Tal vez podríamos vernos cada dos meses», le dijo él, aunque ninguno de los dos cree que sea fácil.
paragraphs.en: Her parents are getting older and she visits them every week. Her boyfriend, Tomás, has a business in Quito and couldn't move with her. "Maybe we could see each other every two months," he told her, although neither of them thinks it will be easy.

paragraphs.es: Anoche llamó a su mejor amiga para pedirle un consejo. «Yo que tú, aceptaría», le dijo su amiga. «Puedes probar durante un año. Si no te gusta, siempre podrás volver.» Camila todavía no ha decidido. La empresa quiere que responda antes del viernes, así que hoy hablará con sus padres. No cree que le pidan que se quede, pero necesita escucharlos.
paragraphs.en: Last night she called her best friend to ask for advice. "If I were you, I'd accept," her friend said. "You can try it for a year. If you don't like it, you can always come back." Camila still hasn't decided. The company wants her to answer before Friday, so today she'll talk to her parents. She doesn't think they'll ask her to stay, but she needs to hear them out.

questions.q: ¿Qué ventaja tiene el trabajo en Panamá?
questions.en: What advantage does the job in Panama have?
questions.why: The conditional shows what would happen if she took the job.

questions.q: ¿Por qué no puede ir Tomás con Camila?
questions.en: Why can't Tomás go with Camila?
choices: Porque tiene un negocio en Quito
questions.answer: Porque tiene un negocio en Quito
questions.why: His business keeps him in Quito.

questions.en: What does Camila's friend think?
questions.why: "Yo que tú, aceptaría" is a common way to give advice.

questions.en: What does the company want?
questions.why: "Quiere que responda antes del viernes."

questions.en: What is Camila going to do today?
questions.why: She hasn't decided yet, so today she'll talk to her parents.

paragraphs.es: Una antigua leyenda de México cuenta que, al principio, las personas solo comían raíces y animales pequeños, y muchas veces pasaban hambre. El dios Quetzalcóatl quería ayudarlas, pero no sabía dónde encontrar un alimento mejor.
paragraphs.en: An old legend from Mexico says that, in the beginning, people only ate roots and small animals, and they often went hungry. The god Quetzalcóatl wanted to help them, but he didn't know where to find a better food.

paragraphs.es: Un día vio a una hormiga roja que llevaba un grano de maíz. Le preguntó de dónde lo había sacado, pero la hormiga no quiso contestar. Quetzalcóatl insistió tanto que, por fin, ella le mostró el camino hacia una montaña enorme, donde estaba guardado el maíz. El camino era tan estrecho que ningún dios podía pasar.
paragraphs.en: One day he saw a red ant carrying a grain of corn. He asked her where she had gotten it, but the ant refused to answer. Quetzalcóatl insisted so much that, at last, she showed him the path to an enormous mountain, where the corn was stored. The path was so narrow that no god could get through.

paragraphs.es: Entonces Quetzalcóatl se convirtió en una hormiga negra y siguió a la hormiga roja por un túnel largo y oscuro. Cuando llegó, tomó un grano de maíz y se lo llevó a los dioses, que lo probaron y se lo dieron a las personas.
paragraphs.en: So Quetzalcóatl turned himself into a black ant and followed the red ant through a long, dark tunnel. When he arrived, he took a grain of corn and carried it to the gods, who tasted it and gave it to the people.

paragraphs.es: Desde entonces, el maíz ha sido la base de la comida mexicana. Quizás por eso, cuando alguien prepara tortillas o tamales, sigue repitiendo una historia de miles de años, aunque no la conozca.
paragraphs.en: Since then, corn has been the foundation of Mexican food. Maybe that's why, when someone makes tortillas or tamales, they're still repeating a story thousands of years old, even if they don't know it.

questions.en: What did people eat in the beginning?
questions.why: They only had roots and small animals, and they often went hungry.

questions.q: ¿Quién le dio la pista a Quetzalcóatl?
questions.en: Who gave Quetzalcóatl the clue?
questions.why: He saw a red ant carrying a grain of corn.

questions.en: Where was the corn stored?
questions.why: The ant showed him the path to an enormous mountain.

questions.en: Why did he turn into an ant?
choices: Porque el camino era muy estrecho
Porque le tenía miedo a la hormiga
questions.answer: Porque el camino era muy estrecho
questions.why: The path was so narrow that no god could get through.

questions.q: Según el texto, ¿qué ha sido el maíz desde entonces?
questions.en: According to the text, what has corn been since then?
choices: La base de la comida mexicana
Un alimento solo para los dioses
questions.answer: La base de la comida mexicana
questions.why: "Ha sido la base de la comida mexicana."

paragraphs.es: Querida Ana: Me pediste mi receta de arroz con pollo, así que aquí está. Es fácil, pero lee todo antes de empezar y no tengas prisa.
paragraphs.en: Dear Ana: You asked me for my chicken and rice recipe, so here it is. It's easy, but read everything before you start and don't rush.

paragraphs.es: Primero, lava bien el pollo y córtalo en pedazos con un cuchillo grande. Pon un poco de aceite en una olla y enciende la estufa. Pica una cebolla y dos dientes de ajo y cocínalos unos minutos en el aceite. Después, añade el pollo y la sal.
paragraphs.en: First, wash the chicken well and cut it into pieces with a big knife. Put a little oil in a pot and turn on the stove. Chop an onion and two cloves of garlic and cook them in the oil for a few minutes. Then add the chicken and the salt.

paragraphs.es: Cuando el pollo esté listo, echa el arroz y el agua, tapa la olla y baja el fuego. No abras la olla y no toques el arroz: ten paciencia. En veinte minutos, más o menos, la comida va a estar lista. Sírvela en platos grandes y come despacio.
paragraphs.en: When the chicken is ready, add the rice and the water, cover the pot and turn down the heat. Don't open the pot and don't touch the rice: be patient. In twenty minutes, more or less, the food will be ready. Serve it on big plates and eat slowly.

paragraphs.es: Y una cosa más: después de comer, lava la olla, el sartén y los cuchillos. ¡No dejes la cocina sucia como la última vez! Llámame el domingo y dime cómo te quedó. Un abrazo, tu abuela Inés.
paragraphs.en: And one more thing: after eating, wash the pot, the frying pan and the knives. Don't leave the kitchen dirty like last time! Call me on Sunday and tell me how it turned out. A hug, your grandma Inés.

questions.q: ¿Qué le pide la abuela a Ana antes de empezar?
questions.en: What does the grandmother ask Ana to do before she starts?
questions.why: Lee todo antes de empezar: read everything before you start.

questions.q: ¿Qué cocina Ana primero en el aceite?
questions.en: What does Ana cook first in the oil?
questions.why: The onion and garlic go in the oil first. The chicken comes after, and the rice last.

questions.q: ¿Qué no debe hacer Ana mientras se cocina el arroz?
questions.en: What shouldn't Ana do while the rice cooks?
questions.why: No abras la olla y no toques el arroz. Negative tú commands take the subjunctive form: no abras, no toques.

questions.en: What happened last time?
choices: Ana no llamó a su abuela
questions.why: ¡No dejes la cocina sucia como la última vez! So last time she left it dirty.

paragraphs.es: Hola, mamá: Ya he terminado mi primer mes en la empresa y quiero contarte cómo me ha ido. Hasta ahora, todo ha sido muy interesante. He conocido a mucha gente y he aprendido más que en toda mi carrera.
paragraphs.en: Hi, Mom: I've now finished my first month at the company and I want to tell you how it's gone. So far, everything has been very interesting. I've met lots of people and I've learned more than in my whole degree.

paragraphs.es: Esta semana he tenido mi primera reunión importante. Mi jefa me ha pedido un informe sobre un proyecto nuevo y lo he escrito yo solo. Todavía no me ha dicho qué piensa, pero creo que le ha gustado.
paragraphs.en: This week I've had my first important meeting. My boss has asked me for a report on a new project and I've written it on my own. She still hasn't told me what she thinks, but I think she liked it.

paragraphs.es: También he cometido algunos errores. El martes envié un correo a la persona equivocada. ¡Qué vergüenza! Pero mi jefa me ha dicho que todos se equivocan al principio y que lo importante es ser responsable.
paragraphs.en: I've also made a few mistakes. On Tuesday I sent an email to the wrong person. How embarrassing! But my boss has told me that everyone makes mistakes at first and that what matters is being responsible.

paragraphs.es: Sé que no ha sido fácil para ti tenerme lejos. Todavía no he decidido si voy a volver a Arequipa en diciembre, pero ya he comprado el boleto para tu cumpleaños. Un beso, Diego.
paragraphs.en: I know it hasn't been easy for you having me far away. I still haven't decided whether I'm going back to Arequipa in December, but I've already bought the ticket for your birthday. A kiss, Diego.

questions.q: ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva Diego en la empresa?
questions.en: How long has Diego been at the company?
questions.why: Ya he terminado mi primer mes: he has just finished his first month.

questions.en: What has his boss asked him for?
choices: Un informe sobre un proyecto nuevo
questions.answer: Un informe sobre un proyecto nuevo
questions.why: Mi jefa me ha pedido un informe sobre un proyecto nuevo, and he wrote it on his own.

questions.en: What mistake did Diego make on Tuesday?
choices: Envió un correo a la persona equivocada
questions.answer: Envió un correo a la persona equivocada
questions.why: El martes envié un correo a la persona equivocada. A finished moment on a named day takes the preterite: envié, not he enviado.

questions.en: What hasn't Diego decided yet?
choices: Si va a volver a Arequipa en diciembre
Si va a comprar el boleto
questions.answer: Si va a volver a Arequipa en diciembre
questions.why: Todavía no he decidido si voy a volver a Arequipa en diciembre. The ticket for his mom's birthday he has already bought.

paragraphs.es: ¿Cómo será mi vida dentro de diez años? Es difícil saberlo, pero tengo algunos planes. Primero, terminaré la universidad. Estudiaré derecho, porque mi sueño es ser abogada como mi tía. Tal vez viviré en Managua, o quizás en otro país.
paragraphs.en: What will my life be like ten years from now? It's hard to know, but I have some plans. First, I'll finish university. I'll study law, because my dream is to be a lawyer like my aunt. Maybe I'll live in Managua, or perhaps in another country.

paragraphs.es: Mi hermano dice que nunca saldré de León, porque me encanta mi ciudad. A lo mejor tiene razón. Si me quedo aquí, abriré una oficina pequeña y ayudaré a la gente del barrio.
paragraphs.en: My brother says I'll never leave León, because I love my city. Maybe he's right. If I stay here, I'll open a small office and help the people in the neighborhood.

paragraphs.es: Mi amiga Valentina tiene otros planes. Ella dice que con mucho dinero compraría una casa en la playa, viajaría por todo el mundo y nunca trabajaría. Yo no haría eso, porque me aburriría. Pero me gustaría tener tiempo para visitar a mi familia y para cuidar el planeta.
paragraphs.en: My friend Valentina has other plans. She says that with a lot of money she'd buy a house on the beach, travel all over the world and never work. I wouldn't do that, because I'd get bored. But I'd like to have time to visit my family and to take care of the planet.

paragraphs.es: No sé si todo será posible. Pero de una cosa estoy segura: dentro de diez años, todavía tendré este cuaderno.
paragraphs.en: I don't know if it will all be possible. But I'm sure of one thing: ten years from now, I'll still have this notebook.

questions.q: ¿Qué quiere estudiar la persona que escribe?
questions.en: What does the writer want to study?
questions.why: Estudiaré derecho, porque mi sueño es ser abogada: she'll study law to become a lawyer like her aunt.

questions.q: ¿Qué hará si se queda en León?
questions.en: What will she do if she stays in León?
choices: Comprará una casa en la playa
questions.why: Si me quedo aquí, abriré una oficina pequeña. The house on the beach and the travel are Valentina's ideas.

questions.en: What would Valentina do with a lot of money?
questions.why: She'd buy a house on the beach, travel and never work. The conditional (trabajaría) is for what she'd do, not what she will do.

questions.q: ¿Por qué la persona que escribe no haría lo mismo que Valentina?
questions.en: Why wouldn't the writer do the same as Valentina?
choices: Porque no le gusta la playa
questions.why: Yo no haría eso, porque me aburriría: she'd get bored.

paragraphs.es: Ramón vive en Cuenca y lleva tres días con tos, fiebre y dolor de garganta. Su esposa quiere que vaya al médico, pero a él no le gustan los médicos. Al final, el jueves pide una cita.
paragraphs.en: Ramón lives in Cuenca and has had a cough, a fever and a sore throat for three days. His wife wants him to go to the doctor, but he doesn't like doctors. In the end, on Thursday he makes an appointment.

paragraphs.es: La doctora lo examina y le dice: «Usted tiene gripe. No es nada grave, pero es importante que descanse unos días y que beba mucha agua. Le recomiendo que no vaya a trabajar hasta el lunes». Luego le da una receta para una medicina.
paragraphs.en: The doctor examines him and tells him, "You have the flu. It's nothing serious, but it's important that you rest for a few days and drink lots of water. I recommend you don't go to work until Monday." Then she gives him a prescription for some medicine.

paragraphs.es: Ramón no está contento. «Doctora, tengo mucho trabajo. ¿Es necesario que me quede en casa?». «Sí», contesta ella. «No quiero que sus compañeros se enfermen también».
paragraphs.en: Ramón isn't happy. "Doctor, I have a lot of work. Is it necessary for me to stay home?" "Yes," she answers. "I don't want your coworkers to get sick too."

paragraphs.es: En casa, su esposa le prepara una sopa de pollo y le dice: «Ojalá te mejores pronto. Y la próxima vez, espero que me hagas caso desde el primer día». Ramón se ríe, toma la medicina y se va a dormir.
paragraphs.en: At home, his wife makes him chicken soup and tells him, "I hope you feel better soon. And next time, I hope you listen to me from the first day." Ramón laughs, takes the medicine and goes to sleep.

words.en: listen to, pay attention to (hacer caso)

questions.en: What does Ramón's wife want?
questions.why: Su esposa quiere que vaya al médico. Querer que + a different subject takes the subjunctive: vaya.

questions.en: What does his wife hope for next time?

Que la doctora venga a casa
questions.answer: Que Ramón le haga caso desde el primer día
questions.why: Espero que me hagas caso desde el primer día: she hopes he'll listen to her from day one.

paragraphs.es: Joaquín está enamorado de Isabel, una compañera de su clase en Santiago, pero tiene miedo de hablar con ella. No cree que ella sienta lo mismo, y le da vergüenza acercarse. Cada vez que la ve, se pone rojo.
paragraphs.en: Joaquín is in love with Isabel, a classmate of his in Santiago, but he's afraid to talk to her. He doesn't think she feels the same, and he's too embarrassed to go up to her. Every time he sees her, he turns red.

paragraphs.es: Su mejor amiga, Josefina, está segura de que Isabel también lo quiere. «Es obvio que le gustas», le dice. «Siempre se sienta a tu lado. Dudo que sea casualidad». Pero Joaquín no está convencido. «Es raro que nunca me hable», contesta.
paragraphs.en: His best friend, Josefina, is sure that Isabel likes him too. "It's obvious she likes you," she tells him. "She always sits next to you. I doubt it's a coincidence." But Joaquín isn't convinced. "It's strange that she never talks to me," he answers.

paragraphs.es: Josefina pierde la paciencia. «Mira, a menos que hables con ella, nunca vas a saber la verdad. Habla con ella antes de que termine el año. No vas a morir de vergüenza, te lo prometo».
paragraphs.en: Josefina loses her patience. "Look, unless you talk to her, you'll never know the truth. Talk to her before the year ends. You're not going to die of embarrassment, I promise."

paragraphs.es: El viernes, después de clase, Joaquín por fin le pregunta a Isabel si quiere tomar un helado con él. Ella sonríe: «¡Me alegra que por fin me lo preguntes! Pensaba que nunca ibas a hablar conmigo». Desde lejos, Josefina está muy orgullosa.
paragraphs.en: On Friday, after class, Joaquín finally asks Isabel if she wants to get ice cream with him. She smiles: "I'm glad you finally asked me! I thought you were never going to talk to me." From a distance, Josefina is very proud.

questions.q: ¿Por qué Joaquín no habla con Isabel?
questions.en: Why doesn't Joaquín talk to Isabel?
choices: Tiene miedo y le da vergüenza
questions.answer: Tiene miedo y le da vergüenza
questions.why: He's afraid, and he doesn't think she feels the same: no cree que ella sienta lo mismo. Doubt takes the subjunctive.

questions.en: What does Josefina think?

Que Isabel quiere a otro chico
Que Joaquín no debe hablar con Isabel
questions.answer: Que es obvio que Isabel quiere a Joaquín
questions.why: Es obvio que le gustas. Certainty (es obvio que) takes the indicative: gustas, not gustes.

questions.q: ¿Cuándo debe hablar Joaquín con Isabel, según Josefina?

choices: Antes de que termine el año
questions.answer: Antes de que termine el año

questions.en: How does Isabel react?
questions.why: ¡Me alegra que por fin me lo preguntes! An emotion (me alegra que) takes the subjunctive: preguntes.

paragraphs.es: Ayer fue un día de esos. A las seis de la mañana se fue la luz, así que no sonó el despertador. Me desperté tarde, me vestí a oscuras y salí corriendo, porque tenía prisa. En el metro me di cuenta: se me olvidó la billetera en la casa.
paragraphs.en: Yesterday was one of those days. At six in the morning the power went out, so the alarm didn't go off. I woke up late, got dressed in the dark and ran out, because I was in a hurry. On the subway I realized: I'd forgotten my wallet at home.

paragraphs.es: Llegué a la oficina media hora tarde. Mi jefe me miró, pero solo dijo: «Más vale tarde que nunca». A la hora del almuerzo, mi compañera Marta me contó que nuestro jefe va a dejar la empresa. —¡No me digas! —le contesté.
paragraphs.en: I got to the office half an hour late. My boss looked at me, but only said, "Better late than never." At lunchtime, my coworker Marta told me that our boss is going to leave the company. "You don't say!" I answered.

paragraphs.es: Yo quería su puesto, pero Lupita lo pidió primero. Como dice mi abuela, camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente. ¡Qué lástima!
paragraphs.en: I wanted his job, but Lupita asked for it first. As my grandmother says, you snooze, you lose. What a shame!

paragraphs.es: Por la tarde empezó a llover y yo no tenía paraguas. Ni modo: al mal tiempo, buena cara. Llegué a la casa mojado, pero mi hija me esperaba con un chocolate caliente. Al final, el día no fue tan malo.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon it started to rain and I didn't have an umbrella. Oh well: you have to make the best of it. I got home wet, but my daughter was waiting for me with a hot chocolate. In the end, the day wasn't so bad.

words.en: oh well, nothing to be done
make the best of a bad situation

questions.en: Why didn't the alarm go off?
questions.why: Se fue la luz: the power went out at six in the morning.

questions.why: Se me olvidó la billetera en la casa. He didn't have an umbrella either, but that comes later.

questions.q: ¿Qué quiere decir «camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente» aquí?
questions.en: What does «camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente» mean here?
choices: Lupita pidió el puesto antes que él
El jefe se durmió en la oficina
questions.answer: Lupita pidió el puesto antes que él
questions.why: The shrimp that falls asleep gets carried off by the current: he waited, and Lupita asked for the job first.

questions.en: What does «ni modo» mean?
choices: Oh well, there's nothing to be done
No way, I don't believe it
questions.answer: Oh well, there's nothing to be done
questions.why: Ni modo, common in Mexico, accepts something you can't change, like rain with no umbrella. «¡No me digas!» is the one for surprise.

paragraphs.es: El año pasado, varias escuelas de Montevideo decidieron que los estudiantes dejaran el celular en una caja al entrar a clase. Al principio, muchos padres se quejaron, porque temían que sus hijos no pudieran comunicarse con ellos en caso de emergencia. Hoy, sin embargo, la mayoría de los maestros dice que la medida ha funcionado mejor de lo que esperaban.
paragraphs.en: Last year, several schools in Montevideo decided that students should leave their cell phones in a box when they came into class. At first, many parents complained, because they were afraid their children wouldn't be able to reach them in an emergency. Today, however, most teachers say the measure has worked better than they expected.

paragraphs.es: Según la directora de un liceo del centro, los recreos cambiaron casi de inmediato. «Antes, los chicos se sentaban en el patio, cada uno mirando su pantalla. Ahora juegan, discuten y hasta se aburren. Y aburrirse también es necesario», explica. Algunos profesores añaden que los alumnos se concentran más y que las peleas por mensajes o fotos han disminuido.
paragraphs.en: According to the principal of a high school downtown, recess changed almost immediately. "Before, the kids sat in the schoolyard, each one looking at their screen. Now they play, argue and even get bored. And getting bored is necessary too," she explains. Some teachers add that students concentrate more and that fights over messages or photos have gone down.

paragraphs.es: No todos están de acuerdo. Un grupo de estudiantes le escribió una carta al periódico en la que decía que prohibir el teléfono era tratarlos como niños. «Si nos enseñaran a usarlo bien, no haría falta esconderlo», afirmaba la carta. Para ellos, el celular también es una herramienta: sirve para buscar información, traducir una palabra o grabar una explicación.
paragraphs.en: Not everyone agrees. A group of students wrote a letter to the newspaper saying that banning phones was treating them like children. "If they taught us to use it well, there'd be no need to hide it," the letter said. For them, the cell phone is also a tool: it's useful for looking up information, translating a word or recording an explanation.

paragraphs.es: Quizás los dos lados tengan algo de razón. Prohibir es más fácil que enseñar, pero enseñar lleva tiempo, y las escuelas rara vez lo tienen. Lo ideal sería que la regla no fuera el final de la conversación, sino el principio. Si dentro de unos años los estudiantes saben cuándo guardar el teléfono sin que nadie se lo pida, la medida habrá cumplido su objetivo.
paragraphs.en: Maybe both sides are partly right. Banning is easier than teaching, but teaching takes time, and schools rarely have it. Ideally, the rule wouldn't be the end of the conversation, but the beginning. If in a few years students know when to put their phones away without anyone asking them, the measure will have done its job.

Cuando los padres estén de acuerdo
questions.answer: Cuando los estudiantes guarden el teléfono solos
questions.why: Its goal is that students put their phones away without anyone asking them.

paragraphs.es: Cuando Diego se mudó de Lima a Buenos Aires, pensaba que no tendría problemas con el idioma. Al fin y al cabo, allí también se hablaba español. Pero el primer día, en la oficina, un compañero le preguntó: «Che, ¿vos de dónde sos?», y Diego tardó unos segundos en entender que solo quería saber de dónde era.
paragraphs.en: When Diego moved from Lima to Buenos Aires, he thought he wouldn't have any trouble with the language. After all, they spoke Spanish there too. But on the first day at the office, a coworker asked him, "Che, ¿vos de dónde sos?", and it took Diego a few seconds to understand that he only wanted to know where he was from.

paragraphs.es: En Argentina, como en Uruguay y en buena parte de Centroamérica, mucha gente usa vos en lugar de tú, y algunos verbos cambian un poco: vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos. «Che» sirve para llamar la atención de alguien, más o menos como «oye». Y al trabajo muchos le dicen laburo, una palabra que llegó con los inmigrantes italianos hace más de un siglo.
paragraphs.en: In Argentina, as in Uruguay and much of Central America, many people use vos instead of tú, and some verbs change a little: vos tenés, vos querés, vos sos. "Che" is used to get someone's attention, more or less like "oye". And many people call work laburo, a word that arrived with Italian immigrants more than a century ago.

paragraphs.es: Durante las primeras semanas, Diego apuntaba en el celular cada palabra nueva. Aprendió que el colectivo es el autobús, que la birome es el bolígrafo y que, si alguien dice que algo está «re lindo», quiere decir que es muy bonito. También descubrió que, aunque llegara tarde a una cena, nadie se enojaba, porque casi nadie llegaba a la hora.
paragraphs.en: During the first few weeks, Diego wrote down every new word on his phone. He learned that a colectivo is a bus, that a birome is a ballpoint pen, and that if someone says something is "re lindo", they mean it's very pretty. He also found out that even if he got to a dinner late, nobody got annoyed, because hardly anyone arrived on time.

paragraphs.es: Seis meses después, su mamá lo llamó desde Lima y se rio al escucharlo. «Hijo, ¿desde cuándo hablas así?», le preguntó. Diego no se había dado cuenta de que había empezado a decir «che» sin pensarlo. Le dijo que no se preocupara, que seguía siendo el mismo de siempre, aunque ahora tomara mate todas las mañanas con sus compañeros del laburo.
paragraphs.en: Six months later, his mom called him from Lima and laughed when she heard him. "Son, since when do you talk like that?" she asked. Diego hadn't noticed that he'd started saying "che" without thinking about it. He told her not to worry, that he was still the same as always, even if he now drank mate every morning with his coworkers.

paragraphs.es: Durante siglos, los pescadores del lago Cocibolca, en Nicaragua, contaban que en sus aguas vivían tiburones. Los científicos que visitaban el país no les creían. Era imposible, decían, que un tiburón viviera en agua dulce, tan lejos del mar. Muchos pensaban que los pescadores habían confundido a los tiburones con otro pez grande, o que exageraban, como suele pasar con las historias de pescadores.
paragraphs.en: For centuries, fishermen on Lake Cocibolca, in Nicaragua, said that sharks lived in its waters. The scientists who visited the country didn't believe them. It was impossible, they said, for a shark to live in fresh water, so far from the sea. Many thought the fishermen had mistaken the sharks for some other big fish, or that they were exaggerating, as tends to happen with fishermen's stories.

paragraphs.es: Sin embargo, los pescadores tenían razón. En los años sesenta, un grupo de investigadores marcó a cientos de tiburones en el lago y, con el tiempo, volvió a encontrar a algunos de ellos en el mar Caribe. Así comprobaron que los animales no se habían quedado atrapados en el lago, como se había creído, sino que viajaban por el río San Juan, subiendo los rápidos casi como lo hacen los salmones.
paragraphs.en: However, the fishermen were right. In the sixties, a group of researchers tagged hundreds of sharks in the lake and, over time, found some of them again in the Caribbean Sea. That's how they proved that the animals hadn't been trapped in the lake, as had been believed, but traveled along the San Juan River, going up the rapids almost the way salmon do.

paragraphs.es: Se trataba del tiburón toro, una especie que puede pasar del agua salada al agua dulce sin problemas. Hoy se sabe que también sube por otros ríos de América.
paragraphs.en: It was the bull shark, a species that can move from salt water to fresh water without trouble. Today it's known that it also swims up other rivers in the Americas.

paragraphs.es: La historia no tiene un final feliz. Durante años, se pagó por cada tiburón que se sacara del lago, y se pescaron tantos que hoy casi no se ven. Si se hubiera escuchado antes a los pescadores, quizás se habría entendido a tiempo lo que estaba en juego. Ahora, algunos biólogos esperan que, si se protege el río, los tiburones vuelvan algún día a las aguas donde nadie creía que pudieran vivir.
paragraphs.en: The story doesn't have a happy ending. For years, money was paid for every shark taken out of the lake, and so many were caught that today they're hardly ever seen. If people had listened to the fishermen sooner, maybe they would have understood in time what was at stake. Now, some biologists hope that, if the river is protected, the sharks will one day come back to the waters where no one believed they could live.

questions.en: Why didn't the scientists believe the fishermen?

questions.why: "Era imposible que un tiburón viviera en agua dulce": the imperfect subjunctive after a judgment in the past.

questions.answer: Que los tiburones viajaban entre el lago y el mar

paragraphs.es: Cuando murió mi abuela, encontramos en su armario una caja de zapatos llena de cartas. Todas estaban escritas por la misma persona, un tal Rafael, y habían sido enviadas desde Santiago de Cuba entre 1958 y 1961. Ninguno de nosotros había oído hablar de él. Mi madre, que siempre había creído conocer todos los secretos de la familia, se quedó callada un buen rato.
paragraphs.en: When my grandmother died, we found a shoebox full of letters in her closet. They were all written by the same person, a certain Rafael, and had been sent from Santiago de Cuba between 1958 and 1961. None of us had ever heard of him. My mother, who had always thought she knew all the family's secrets, was quiet for a good while.

paragraphs.es: Leímos las cartas una noche, en la cocina. Rafael y mi abuela se habían conocido en un baile cuando ella tenía diecisiete años. Él le pedía que lo esperara, porque pensaba ahorrar dinero para mudarse a La Habana y casarse con ella. En la última carta le decía que, si las cosas no cambiaban pronto, se iría a vivir con un tío a Venezuela, y que le escribiría en cuanto llegara.
paragraphs.en: We read the letters one night, in the kitchen. Rafael and my grandmother had met at a dance when she was seventeen. He asked her to wait for him, because he planned to save money to move to Havana and marry her. In the last letter he told her that, if things didn't change soon, he'd go live with an uncle in Venezuela, and that he'd write to her as soon as he arrived.

paragraphs.es: Pero nunca volvió a escribir, o, si lo hizo, sus cartas no llegaron. Un año después, mi abuela se casó con mi abuelo, con quien vivió cincuenta años y tuvo cuatro hijos. Nunca le contó a nadie lo de Rafael. Tal vez pensó que no valía la pena, o tal vez temía que alguien la juzgara.
paragraphs.en: But he never wrote again, or, if he did, his letters never arrived. A year later, my grandmother married my grandfather, with whom she lived for fifty years and had four children. She never told anyone about Rafael. Maybe she thought it wasn't worth it, or maybe she was afraid someone would judge her.

paragraphs.es: Mi madre dice que, si la abuela hubiera querido olvidarlo, habría quemado las cartas. No sabemos por qué las guardó durante más de sesenta años. Lo que sí sabemos es que, al final de cada carta, Rafael escribía la misma frase: «No me olvides, aunque la vida nos lleve por caminos distintos». Y, de algún modo, ella nunca lo olvidó.
paragraphs.en: My mother says that if Grandma had wanted to forget him, she would have burned the letters. We don't know why she kept them for more than sixty years. What we do know is that at the end of every letter, Rafael wrote the same sentence: "Don't forget me, even if life takes us down different paths." And, somehow, she never forgot him.

questions.q: ¿Qué encontraron en el armario de la abuela?
questions.en: What did they find in the grandmother's closet?
questions.why: A shoebox full of letters, all from Rafael.

questions.q: ¿Cómo se conocieron Rafael y la abuela?
questions.en: How did Rafael and the grandmother meet?

questions.q: ¿Qué le pedía Rafael a la abuela?
questions.en: What did Rafael ask the grandmother?
